macro.regime: Hawkish-Fed overheating-and-tariff-shock crosscurrent inside a widening credit-bifurcation regime
macro.narrative: As of the Wed 25 Nov US close, the macro data cluster came in uniformly hot: core PCE rose to 3.3% y/y (a 3-year high, above the 3.2% consensus), Q3 GDP was revised sharply up to 4.3% (vs 3.5% consensus), initial jobless claims fell to 189k (matching the lowest since 1969 outside this July), and CB consumer confidence surged 11.4pts to 103.3 (vs 92.4 consensus, best since Jan 2025) -- an unambiguously 'too-hot' economy. That print landed the same day Trump unveiled new tariffs on 16 trading partners (China, EU, India, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan and others) to replace the Supreme-Court-struck IEEPA duties, and together they triggered a textbook good-news-is-bad-news air pocket -- the S&P 500 fell as much as ~3.2% intraday before closing just -0.25% at 7182.78 (Nasdaq -0.62%, Dow +0.33%, Russell +0.71%, VIX +7.32% to 28.29, still well above the pre-crash 15-18 range). The Fed's internal split widened in response: Governor Waller is now publicly floating a 50bp 'shock' hike for Dec 9, while NY Fed's Williams pushed back against 'dramatic action' -- Kalshi/Polymarket still price ~93-96% odds of a 25bp hike (little moved from Tuesday), but the tail risk of a larger move is now explicitly on the table. Credit continued to bifurcate rather than heal: CCC-rated spreads widened further to roughly 1,400bp (the CCC-BB gap now the widest in three years) even as broad HY OAS held near 363bp, still contained in BB/B -- the Goldman-flagged stress remains concentrated, not systemic, but is getting worse at the margin. Gold/silver/miners staged a sharp reversal of Tuesday's selloff (GLD +0.61% to $327.45, SLV +0.71% to $37.10, GDX +3.53%, gold futures +1.57% to ~$3617.80) on what looks like tariff-shock safe-haven demand overriding the hawkish real-yield repricing, while oil got a geopolitical bid from the Houthis' claimed Ras Tanura refinery strike (WTI +2.56% to ~$84.15) even as Brent (-0.63% to ~$90.82) stayed anchored to the supply-glut narrative ahead of OPEC+'s pivotal Nov 29 Vienna meeting on 2027 quotas (Iraq/Kazakhstan capacity disputes, UAE no longer quota-bound, IEA still flagging a ~1.7mb/d Q4 surplus). The China rare-earth/tariff truce remains intact (export-curb suspension confirmed extended to Jan 27 2027) and Taiwan tension sits at a steady-state drumbeat (Taiwan's premier reiterating 'reunification is not an option', no fresh PLA war-games since Dec 2025) -- net, the base case stays a choppy, rotation-heavy tape, now complicated by a genuinely overheating US economy forcing a hawkish Fed into a fresh tariff shock rather than the cleaner 'stagnant growth plus inflation' stagflation framing used earlier this week.
